data: Are the attention weights obtained by senti-emoji embedding and word-emoji embedding across words different?

The question asks whether the attention weights obtained by senti-emoji embedding and word-emoji embedding across words are different. From the analysis of the figure:

1. The figure shows two lines representing ATT-E (blue) and MATT-BIE (orange).
2. The y-axis represents the attention weights.
3. The x-axis represents the words in the tweet context.
4. The blue line (ATT-E) and the orange line (MATT-BIE) intersect at the beginning but diverge significantly after the first few words.
5. The orange line (MATT-BIE) has higher values than the blue line (ATT-E) for most of the words shown.

Based on this analysis, the attention weights obtained by senti-emoji embedding and word-emoji embedding across words are indeed different.
